title: RBAC v2 fast-path policy pipeline and explainable deny reasoning
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Deliver a high-throughput, low-latency authorization evaluation pipeline for RBAC v2 that supports API/runtime/console traffic. The goal is a fast-path for common allow/deny decisions using a sharded, indexed policy cache and vectorized matchers, plus an explainable deny-reason generator that surfaces minimal, human-readable rationale for admin UIs and audit logs. This ticket scopes the pipeline implementation, integration with the authorization middleware, and the audit enrichment for deny explanations.
updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created with initial design goals and performance targets (tail latency < 20ms P95 for simple allow checks at 99th percentile load).

2025-02-18: Spike completed - benchmarked in-memory rule index using prefix trees and attribute-hash maps; achieved ~12ms median, ~28ms P95 in microbenchmarks. Notes: KV cache eviction needs tuning for multi-tenant churn.

2025-02-21: Design review with PM and Security. Decided to separate fast-path (exact-match + role-bind cache) from slow-path (policy expression eval). Security requested explicit explainable deny payload schema for audit ingestion.

2025-02-24: Prototype middleware shim implemented in the runtime gateway. It checks fast-path cache first, emits telemetry, and falls back to policy engine. Added unit tests for cache consistency across shard ownership changes.

2025-02-28: UX sync: Console team requested deny reasons to include related policy id, matched attributes, and suggested remediations. Agreed to cap explainable payload size and redact sensitive attribute values before logging.

2025-03-01: Integration tests added for SSO principals with SAML group-to-role mapping. Observed an edge case where long group lists triggered slow attribute normalization; created follow-up ENG-478032 to optimize mapping pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Fast-path decision cache implemented and sharded: consistent hashing across runtime nodes and automated rebalance with zero-downtime cache warmups.
Middleware integrates fast-path and slow-path with request tracing: decision_id present in span and audit records.
Explainable deny generator emits compact JSON payload (policy_id, matched_rules, reason_summary, remediation_hint) with redaction rules applied.
End-to-end latency targets met in benchmark harness: P50 < 10ms, P95 < 25ms for cached decisions at 10k RPS simulated traffic.
Security review completed and approved; deny payload schema certified for GDPR compliance and sensitive-attribute redaction.
Automated tests and a canary rollout plan for Dedicated and Hosted environments are documented in the release playbook.
blockers: Need updated KMS token access for canary environment (SEC-ops ticket opened)
Policy indexer shard rebalance race condition under heavy rule churn - requires a fix in policy-store (ENG-478033)
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on correctness of deny reasoning and redaction logic. Pay attention to multi-tenant cache isolation and telemetry footprint. Performance-sensitive code paths are annotated; prefer non-blocking algorithms and avoid heap allocations per request where possible.
manual_steps: Deploy policy-indexer v2 to canary (policy-store-canary) and verify shard ownership logs
Run canary traffic using authz-loadtest with SAML principal set A and confirm latency and deny-reason sampling
Inspect audit stream in kinesis-dev to ensure deny payloads conform to schema and are redacted
